title: Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa – Pappi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Rabbi Chanina (or Rabbi Chinena) bar Pappa – Pappi. Hyman writes: In the biography of this pious man great confusion has occurred. Yuchasin cites briefly: “Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi, who was saved from the noblewoman … and when he died a pillar of fire separated.” Seder HaDorot criticized it, saying: “Yuchasin omitted mention of Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa; it seems that he holds that Pappa and Pappi are one.” End of quotation. And in Yuchasin HaShalem (London printing)

its words are: “Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi is called Rabbi Chanina Pappi; this one fulfilled the whole Torah, and a noblewoman solicited him; he was a colleague of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi. Rav said to Rav Yehudah: Such as Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi, Rabbi Abbahu and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha … and when he died a pillar of fire separated … until Rabbi Alexandri approached him; and he also lived in Rav Yosef’s time”; and Seder HaDorot cites likewise; see there.

Hyman wonders how scholars of their stature should mix several generations together in a way the mind cannot bear — that one who was a colleague of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi should live in Rav Yosef’s time? All their proof that he was a colleague of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi seems taken from Ketubot 77b, when he asked the Angel of Death for his knife and he said to him, “Do you wish to do as your colleague (Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi)?” What proof is this from the Angel of Death, when the whole incident speaks in riddles? He called him “his colleague”

because this is what happened to the Angel of Death with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi; and it is against explicit Gemara passages, for in truth he was a colleague of all Rabbi Yochanan’s students, and he too received from him, as in Jerusalem Talmud Bava Kamma, beginning of halakhah 2 of chapter 10: “Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa in the name of Rabbi Yochanan.” Likewise he received from Ze’iri, as in Terumot 7:2: “Rabbi Chinena bar Pappa before Ze’iri”; and there, 1:2, “taught before Rabbi Ze’ira” — Hyman says it should read “before

Ze’iri.” The ways of aggadah he received from the great preacher Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani (a student of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi), as in Sheviit 4:3 and the end of chapter 5: “Rabbi Chinena bar Pappa and Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani passed by one who was plowing in the Sabbatical year. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said to him, ‘Yishar’ [well done]. Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa said to him: Did not our master teach us, ‘And the passers-by did not say’ — from here, that it is forbidden to say to those plowing in the Sabbatical year

‘Yishar’? He said to him: You know how to read; you do not know how to expound,” etc. Likewise we find in Sotah 35a and Niddah 20b: “Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa said: Rabbi Shila of Kefar Tamarta expounded.” In Midrash Shmuel 25:2 he spoke in the name of Rabbi Chanina the scribe. He was friendly with all the great students of Rabbi Yochanan, as in Beitzah 38a: “When Rabbi Abba went up,

he found Rabbi Yochanan (Hyman says it should read Rabbi Abbahu, according to the Maharshal’s reading, or Rabbi Avin, according to Dikdukei Soferim), Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha — and some say Rabbi Abbahu, Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi and Rabbi Zeira — and some say Rabbi Abbahu, Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha — sitting and saying.” In Bava Kamma 117b: “Rabbi Abbahu, Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha sat, and Rabbi Ilai sat with them; Rabbi Abba came and asked them … they said to him: Go

to Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim and Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat” (Hyman places this after Rabbi Yochanan’s death, reasoning that Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat had succeeded him as head. The supplied abbreviation בכ״ס remains unresolved). In Ketubot 84b: “Rabbi Abbahu, Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha sat, and Rabbi Abba sat with them … Rabbi Abba said to them: Because they are of the Patriarch’s house, you flatter him?” In Gittin 29b: a man sent a bill of divorce to his wife and said to the agent, “Go give it

to Abba bar Minyomi” … he came and did not find him … he found Rabbi Abbahu, Rabbi Chanina bar “Pappa” and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha, and Rav Safra was sitting with them. Rav Safra said to them: “But the agent …” They were embarrassed. Rava said: “Rav Safra defeated three ordained Rabbis.” Hyman concludes: From this we see clearly that Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa and Pappi are one. In Yevamot 48b: “Rabbi Chanina bar

Pappi, Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha sat at the gate of Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha, sitting and saying,” etc. In Bava Batra 144b, on the law whether a minor has a share where the sons divide: Rabbi Avin, Rabbi Meyasha and Rabbi Yirmeyah with Rabbi Abbahu, Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha. Rabbi Abbahu said to Rabbi Yirmeyah: “Is the halakhah like us or like you?” (Rabbi Yirmeyah) said to him: “Obviously the halakhah is like us, for I am older

than you, and not like you, for you are youngsters.” (Rabbi Abbahu) said to him: “Does the matter depend on age? The matter depends on reasoning.” Hyman writes: I was distressed by this: how is it possible that Rabbi Yirmeyah, who was Rabbi Zeira’s student, was older than Rabbi Abbahu, Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha? Did not Rabbi Abbahu call Rabbi Yirmeyah “my son,” as in Bava Metzia 47b? And Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha was already a great man of the generation

in Rabbi Yochanan’s lifetime. Hyman continues: But I found the true reading in Dikdukei Soferim, which reads the reverse: that Rabbi Yirmeyah asked Rabbi Abbahu, and Rabbi Abbahu answered him, “for I am older than you,” and Rabbi Yirmeyah said to him, “The matter depends on reasoning.” And what it says there, “And what is the reason?” is from Rabbi Yirmeyah’s words. It is no wonder that Rabbi Yirmeyah answered him so, since Rabbi Yirmeyah became the great man of the generation in their days, as explained in his entry.

Likewise Rabbi Zeira was his colleague, for they sat together, as in Beitzah 38a; in Moed Katan 25b, a dispute of Rabbi Zeira and Rabbi Chinena bar Pappa; and Berakhot 5a: “Rabbi Zeira — and some say Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa — said: A person who sells an object, the seller is sad and the buyer happy; but the Holy One, blessed be He, is not so,” etc. In Moed Katan 3:7: Rabbi Chinena bar Pappa went up to Rabbi Tanchum bar Chiyya (who was in mourning); Rabbi Tanchum bar Chiyya said to him:

“Pray for us,” and he did so. In the days of Rav Yosef and Abaye he was already the elder of the generation, and they sought his decision, as in Ketubot 81b, where Rav Yosef and Abaye sent before Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi, and Abaye did not want to accept his answer, and said to Rav Yosef: “Did Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi hang jewels on it?” They sent it before Rav Minyomi son of Rav Nechumi, etc.

He was there among the town’s judges, as in Bava Batra 171b: Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef (who was among the traveling transmitters) had money owed by Rabbi Abba; he came before Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi, etc. In Moed Katan 3:1: Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa ruled that beds should be overturned for one day. According to the testimony of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani, Sheviit 4:3, he was a great expert in Scripture. Likewise we find mostly his precious homilies, as in Berakhot 5a, where he expounded

the verse “For I have given you good teaching”; there, 23a: “Rav Ashi (Hyman says it should read Rabbi Assi, citing Dikdukei Soferim) said — and some say Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa: ‘Guard your feet’ — guard your orifices when you stand in prayer.” There, 35b: “Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa said: Whoever benefits from this world without a blessing is as though he robs the Holy One, blessed be He … as it is said … What is ‘companion of a destroyer’? He is a companion of Jeroboam.” … “Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa posed a contradiction: It is written …

here, when Israel do the will of the Omnipresent,” etc. There, 51a: “He takes it with both hands. Rabbi Chinena bar Pappa said: What is the verse?” etc. Megillah 11a: “Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa opened this introduction from here.” In Chagigah 5a he said: “Whoever does something and regrets it is forgiven at once, as it is said,” etc. In Bava Batra 75a he said: “The Holy One, blessed be He, wished to give Jerusalem by measure,” etc.

In Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 3:4: “Rabbi Chinena bar Pappa said: We went over all of Scripture,” etc. Among those who transmit teachings from him, Hyman names Rabbi Abba bar Minyomi, who taught before him, citing Eruvin 12a; Rabbi Acha bar Pappa in his name, Bava Kamma 80b; Rabbi Ila in his name, Chagigah 21b. Hyman concludes from all his sayings that he was very pious, as is related of him in Kiddushin 39b:

once a noblewoman solicited him … and he fled from her to a certain bathhouse where, when even two entered together, even by day, they would be harmed. The next day the Rabbis said to him: “Who guarded you?” He said to them: “Two of Caesar’s soldiers guarded me all night.” They said to him: “Perhaps a matter of forbidden relations came to your hand and you were saved from it.” There, 81a, it is related that Rav and Rav Yehudah were walking on the road, and a woman was walking before them. Rav said to Rav Yehudah: “Lift your feet

away from Gehinnom.” He said to him: “But did not the Master himself say that with upright people it is fine?” He said to him: “Who says that ‘upright people’ means such as you and me?” “Rather, what? Such as Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi and his colleagues.” Yuchasin and Seder HaDorot thought that all this is Rav’s words, but Hyman argues that this is not true: Rav never saw Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi, who was in the Land of Israel a long time after him. Hyman considers it clear that Rav answered Rav Yehudah only

“Who says that ‘upright people’ means such as you and me?” and the anonymous Gemara asks, “Rather, what?” and they said, “Such as Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi and his colleagues.” In the Jerusalem Talmud, end of Peah, it is related that Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa used to distribute charity at night. Once the chief of the spirits met him and said to him: “Did not our master teach us, ‘Do not encroach on your neighbor’s boundary’?” He said to him: “And is it not written, ‘A gift in secret subdues anger’?” And

the chief of the spirits was subdued by Rabbi Chanina and fled from him. He was so great in the eyes of the people of his generation that his death is related in a wondrous way, as in Ketubot 77b: the Angel of Death was the groomsman of Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa. When he was about to die, they said to the Angel of Death: “Go do his will.” He went to him and appeared to him. He said to him: “Leave me thirty days until I review my learning, for they say: Fortunate is

one who comes here with his learning in his hand.” He left him. After thirty days he went and appeared to him. He said to him: “Show me my place (in the Garden of Eden).” He said to him: “Very well.” He said to him: “Give me your knife, lest you frighten me on the way.” He said to him: “Do you wish to do to me as your colleague (Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi) did?” He said to him: “Bring a Torah scroll and see whether there is anything written in it that I did not fulfill.” He said to him: “Did you attach yourself to those afflicted with ra’atan and occupy yourself with Torah

(like Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi)?” Even so, when he died a pillar of fire separated between him and the world, and there is a tradition that a pillar of fire separates only for one or two in a generation. Rabbi Alexandri approached him and said: “Do it for your own sake” … it withdrew. We find in Shir HaShirim Rabbah 6:5 Rabbi Chama bar Chanina bar Pappa.

notes.text: Whole supplied Hebrew/all24 English units/all current+historical substantive notes and Fable PASS reviewed. Hyman owns Pappa/Pappi identity claims, generations and his reassignment of the final Kidd81a clause to anonymous Gemara; retain his emphatic arguments without presenting them as canonical identity or independently proven dialogue history. His BavaBatra age/speaker reversal is a reported DikdukeiSoferim reading: named Davidson142b has the initial speakers he criticizes; source144b remains alongside the142b comparison, without alleged OCR-history proof. Source בכ״ס is kept visible and unresolved rather than silently asserted as בל״ס/undoubtedly. The Eruvin12a AbbaMinyomi citation remains held with the prior reviewer nonmatch; no claim of absence elsewhere. Root corrects the draft’s binding-of-a-ban: כפיתה here is overturning beds in mourning, confirmed by full supplemental Guggenheimer MoedKatan3:5 paragraph25. Source3:1 remains supplied, and the saved3:1 is not the matching bed paragraph; do not erase that locator. The same paragraph’s later dream/retraction is outside Hyman’s abbreviated quotation, not added to the translation. כיפי in Ket81b is jewels, a rhetorical claim of having enhanced a ruling, not physical stones hung on it; the source phrase is preserved in its question form. Rav instructs Yehudah to hurry away from Gehinnom, not toward it. Kidd39b ends at two and named40a paragraph0 continues soldiers/נושאי קיסר, correcting armor-bearers while preserving source39b. Chief-of-spirits pronouns made explicit: he flees Chanina, not reverse. Source name forms Chanina/Chinena, Pappa/Pappi and reported variants remain distinct; no blanket harmonization. Historical notes/questions preserved; source abbreviations/locator/Eruvin citation remain held. Digital editions are not printed pixels or correction-history proof.

An additional check of the adjacent Davidson Eruvin 12b also did not locate the Abba bar Minyomi teaching-before-him passage. This narrows the checked range only; it does not disprove Hyman’s citation, establish a replacement folio, or remove the source hold.

In the consulted Davidson text of Eruvin 12a, Rav Adda bar Avimi teaches before Rabbi Chanina, alternatively identified there as Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi. Gittin 29b names Abba bar Minyomi in the separate divorce case. The difference in the transmitter’s name at Eruvin 12a remains unresolved. At Bava Batra 142b the parallel passage has the speaker order Hyman challenges; Rashbam explains talya as the son already born, whose additional gift is at issue. Hyman gives 144b here and attributes the reversed speaker order to Dikdukei Soferim. The abbreviation בכ״ס also remains unresolved.

The consulted Yerushalmi Terumot 7:2 reads Zeira in the exchange Hyman gives with Ze’iri. The consulted Beitzah 38a gives two lists of participants, with names that differ from Hyman’s lists. Berakhot 23a reads Rav Ashi in the consulted text; Rabbi Assi is Hyman’s reported correction. The teaching attributed to Shila occurs at Niddah 26a, the Jerusalem measurement passage at Bava Batra 75b, and the “we went over all of Scripture” passage at Yerushalmi Megillah 3:6 in the editions consulted. The parallel versions of the charity story at Yerushalmi Peah 8:8 and Shekalim 5:4 describe the spirit as afraid before it flees, where Hyman’s text describes it as subdued. In the consulted Moed Katan 3:7 passage, Tanchum’s request is followed by Chanina’s response; Hyman paraphrases this as Chanina praying.

Seder HaDorot treats Pappi and Pappa under separate headings and explicitly disputes their identification. It also recounts the Kiddushin exchange as Rav’s words. Hyman argues for identifying the two name forms and gives the final question and answer to the anonymous Gemara. The wording quoted from the London Yuchasin is given as Hyman reports it.

The abbreviated word on Hyman’s printed page 495 is difficult to make out. An earlier reading proposed בל״ס (“without doubt”), while the supplied Hebrew has בכ״ס. Bava Kamma 117b names Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat in the referral. Dating the episode after Rabbi Yochanan’s death is Hyman’s inference.

Hyman’s printed article cites Bava Batra 144b. The parallel is at 142b in the consulted Talmud text and in Dikdukei Soferim, pp. 387–388. The printed column has Rabbi Abbahu address Rabbi Yirmeyah. The facing manuscript column reverses the address, supporting the opening reversal Hyman reports. Hyman’s assignment of the subsequent lines, including “And what is the reason?”, is his interpretation of the exchange.

Hyman’s printed page 496 names Rabbi Abba bar Minyomi here. The printed column of Dikdukei Soferim, Eruvin 12a (p. 34), gives Rav Adda bar Avimi, as does the consulted Talmud text, which says he taught before Rabbi Chanina or, in the alternative reading, Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi. Abba bar Minyomi appears separately in the divorce case at Gittin 29b.
